solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Parish representative a heavy smoker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lay officer elected to look after a parish church
second meaning: a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe, heavy enough in length

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the parish's elected official is someone who smokes a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The smoker is not a person but the thing smoked: a churchwarden is also a long clay pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a lay church officer in an Anglican parish and a long clay tobacco pipe.

clue.text: Bore on the Tube?

parts.note: the bore is the inner diameter of a gun barrel, the tube, not a dull fellow passenger on the London Underground

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a tedious person on London's Tube (Underground railway); the bore is a barrel's width.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre is the internal diameter of a gun barrel, its bore.

clue.text: Junior needing work experience

parts.note: under means lower in rank, junior
to go means to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A young employee who needs some time in a workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work experience' looks like one phrase, but 'work' is wordplay and 'experience' alone is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or endure it.

clue.text: Artist in Cape working with horses

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
on means working, functioning
a stable is a group of racehorses kept together

explanation.surface: A painter in the Cape busy with horses.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was the English landscape painter of The Hay Wain.

clue.text: Soiled pews one sits in? Cleaning products needed

indicators.note: one sits in the rearranged letters, placed inside them
soiled means messed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Church pews are dirty where people sit, so cleaning cloths are called for.
explanation.definitionFit: Wipes are disposable moist cloths used for cleaning.

clue.text: Controlled bullet in rifle

parts.note: ran means controlled, managed
the bullet is slang for the sack, dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: A bullet fired under control from a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' is the verb meaning to search and plunder, not the gun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it thoroughly and steal, to plunder.

clue.text: A quote about old times turned up in curious collection

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the quote word goes about the others, surrounding them

parts.note: to cite is to quote
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A quotation about bygone days found in an odd assortment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OX inside CITE, giving CITOXE; after A, 'turned up' reverses ACITOXE.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are strange or unusual objects, often a collection of foreign curiosities.

clue.text: Gap to close: tile's one missing in Columbia?

parts.note: a space is a gap
shut means close

indicators.note: missing means the named letter is absent

parts.note: the tile, which has one missing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shuttle with a heat-shield tile missing, as on the doomed Columbia.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbia was the NASA orbiter lost in 2003 after damage to its heat-shield tiles; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbia was the first of NASA's reusable orbiters, an example of the craft.

clue.text: Boy breaking bread for French champion

indicators.note: the boy breaks into the bread, so his letters sit inside it

parts.note: pain is the French word for bread
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy tearing into a loaf for a French hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's knights, hence any heroic champion of a cause.

clue.text: She released evil over Republican in police car

indicators.note: the over and the Republican are placed in the police car

parts.note: a panda car is a British police patrol car
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone let wickedness loose and then put a Republican into a squad car.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda (car) is the old British name for a small police patrol car, once painted in black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora opened the forbidden jar and let all the world's ills escape.

clue.text: A cold fish admitting she has fatal flaw

parts.note: a chill is a cold

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the other word goes inside

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A frosty person who lets her in has a deadly weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold fish' looks like a description of an unfriendly person, but the two words do separate jobs; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero Achilles was vulnerable only at his heel, so the phrase means a single weak spot.

clue.text: Show Spartan having whip round

indicators.note: the whip goes round the Spartan word, enclosing it

parts.note: the cat (o' nine tails) is a whip
spartan means austere, bare

explanation.surface: A warrior from Sparta passing a whip about in a display.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment, a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Prodigal son comes first, being submissive

indicators.note: the son is placed at the front of the other word

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
prodigal means lavish, extravagant

explanation.surface: The prodigal son, returning first, now behaves meekly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the parable of the Prodigal Son, but 'Prodigal' is just a synonym for lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish behaviour is servile, like that of a slave, so it is submissive.

clue.text: Such a worker as scribbled notes?

definitions.text: Such a worker as scribbled notes?

indicators.note: scribbled suggests the letters of notes are dashed off in a muddle

explanation.surface: A shorthand typist is exactly the person whose notes look scribbled.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a steno is a stenographer, who takes notes in shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A steno, short for stenographer, is a clerical worker who records dictation in shorthand.

clue.text: Exact money?

parts.note: exact as a verb means to extort, so money exacted by threats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact money' reads like the correct change for a fare; read 'exact' as a verb meaning to demand by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Extorting payment by threatening to reveal secrets is the crime of extortion by threat.

clue.text: One calls to Lower House: planner worried outside!

definitions.note: a lower is something that lows, a cow

indicators.note: the reworked letters lie outside the house abbreviation, surrounding it
worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A planner, anxious, phones the Lower House of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower House' looks like a parliamentary chamber, but a lower is a cow (one that lows); the alpenhorn's call carries across Alpine pastures.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenhorn is a long wooden horn used by Swiss herders to call to cattle.

clue.text: Musical university retired collection broadcast for rock band

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the musical and university together are read in reverse

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical

indicators.note: broadcast means said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a heap is a collection or pile

explanation.surface: A musical university group, now retired, broadcast a collection for a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is a British hard-rock band named after the Dickens villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah Heep is a long-running English hard rock group formed in 1969.

clue.text: Heinous criminal done by own organisation?

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A wicked crime committed from within a company.
explanation.definitionFit: In-house work is carried out by a firm's own staff rather than outsourced.

clue.text: Hunting bird hunting dog

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hawk of the genus Circus that hunts low over open ground
second meaning: a hound bred for hunting hares

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'hunting' makes it read as one creature; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bird of prey that quarters fields and a hare-hunting hound breed.

clue.text: Judgement correct as Tertullus shows

indicators.note: the answer is on display within the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: Tertullus, the orator in Acts, demonstrates sound judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: Tertullus is the lawyer who accuses Paul before Felix in the Book of Acts; here he only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Good taste is discernment in aesthetic matters, a kind of judgement.

clue.text: Engine right inside slow boat in Spain

indicators.note: the right letter goes inside the boat word

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A motor fitted to a slow Spanish vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a rotary engine driven by a flow of steam, water or gas.

clue.text: Drinks lacking body?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: strong distilled alcohol such as gin or whisky
second meaning: ghosts, beings without physical form

explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking body' sounds like a wine-tasting note about thin drinks; it means disembodied beings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both distilled liquors and ghosts or souls without bodies.

clue.text: Garments Trish knitted on back street?

indicators.note: knitted suggests the letters are worked together into a new pattern
back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ST is the address abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Clothes that a woman called Trish knitted, worn on a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' rearranges TRISH to TSHIR; 'back' turns ST into TS.
explanation.definitionFit: T-shirts are casual collarless tops, items of clothing.

clue.text: Second XI shows power

parts.note: eleven players make a team, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: A club's reserve side shows its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is vapour used to drive engines, a source of motive power.

clue.text: Immediately caging rook in Berlin I see!

indicators.note: caging means enclosing, so the rook goes inside

parts.note: now means immediately
R is the chess notation for rook
ich is German for I

explanation.surface: An exclamation from someone in Berlin who has suddenly spotted a caged bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see!' reads as an exclamation, but a see is a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is the seat of an Anglican bishop, and a bishop's diocese is called a see.

clue.text: Educated English lewd about sex?

indicators.note: the lewd word goes about the other, surrounding it

parts.note: rude means lewd, indecent
it is a slang word for sex

explanation.surface: Asking whether a well-schooled Englishman is being crude about sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite means having great learning, well read and scholarly.

clue.text: Opening gold reserve involves one key

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so gold and reserve together take the other letters into their middle

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
ice means coolness or reserve of manner
I is the Roman numeral one
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: Opening a gold store requires one key.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or mouth, an opening in the body or a structure.

clue.text: Diabolical screen wraps around Catholic magicians

indicators.note: the reworked letters wrap the other pieces, enclosing them
diabolical means dreadful, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: C is short for circa, around
Roman is short for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A devilish screen that encloses Catholic sorcerers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is not a container signal here but C, short for circa; Roman alone is a common shorthand for Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Necromancers practise sorcery by summoning the dead, a kind of wizardry.
